info.title: Vukem API
info.description:
The JSON API of Vukem Tools.

Authenticate every call with an API key, either as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or as the `X-API-Key` header. Issue a key with `POST /api/v1/tokens`; it carries only the abilities you asked for, and the secret is shown once.

Errors are RFC 9457 problem documents (`application/problem+json`). A `422` adds an `errors` object mapping each rejected field to its messages.

Rate limits: 120 requests per minute per IP, 60 per minute per key, and 5 key issues per minute per IP. Over the limit is a `429` with `Retry-After`.

See /docs for the reference and https://tools.vukem.dev/docs/api/overview/ for the overview.

get.summary: List the abilities a key may be granted
get.description: The closed set of abilities, so a client does not have to hardcode them.

get.summary: Report which engines this server has and what its limits are
get.description: Every external program, whether it was resolved at startup and the version it reported, plus the registered tools and the numbers this server enforces. An engine the image does not carry hides its tools, and this is where that is visible.
trim keeps one range; split cuts the whole video into consecutive clips.
Every code a failed conversion can carry, with the sentence to show and whether the same input is worth submitting again. Published so a client does not hardcode them.
Newest first. Scoped to the caller: another account's work is never listed.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many to return, 1 to 100. Default 20.

delete.description: Stops a conversion that has not ended and returns it as it now stands. One that already ended is answered 409.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The conversion's id, as returned when it was submitted.

get.description: The polling endpoint: ask for it until status is finished, error or cancelled. A client that can hold a connection open should use the event stream instead.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The conversion's id, as returned when it was submitted.

get.summary: Get signed links to a conversion's result
get.description: Signed, expiring links to the files a finished conversion produced. A link is signed when you ask for it, so it is never older than your request.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The conversion's id, as returned when it was submitted.

post.summary: Start linking a program to an account
post.description: For a program that cannot show a login form, such as a chat bot. Returns a secret device_code to poll with and a short user_code to show the person, who opens verification_url in a browser, checks the code and approves. What the key may do is fixed by the client kind, not asked for. Rate limited per IP.

client.description: The kind of program asking. It decides what the key may do: the server fixes the abilities, the program cannot choose them.

device_name.description: A label for the key in the account's key list, such as the Telegram name of the person. Optional.

post.summary: Collect the key of an approved link
post.description: Poll every `interval` seconds. status is pending until the person decides, then approved with the key (shown once and made at that moment), denied, or expired. A link that never existed reads as expired.

device_code.description: The device_code from the call that started the link.

get.summary: List the platforms a video can be downloaded from
get.description: The closed list. A URL outside it is refused before yt-dlp is started, so this service cannot be used to fetch an arbitrary address.
The account the key belongs to. Useful to check a key is live.
Newest first, revoked keys included. Secrets are never listed.

post.summary: Issue an API key
post.description: Exchanges email and password for an API key limited to the abilities asked for. The secret is returned once and never stored: only its SHA-256 hash is.

abilities.description: What the key may do; GET /api/v1/abilities lists the accepted values.

code.description: A two-factor code, for accounts with two-factor authentication.

device_name.description: A label for this key, shown when listing keys.

recovery_code.description: A two-factor recovery code, instead of code.

delete.summary: Revoke the key used by this request
delete.description: The row is kept for the audit trail, marked revoked.

delete.summary: Revoke one of the caller's keys by id
delete.description: Scoped to the caller: another account's key id is answered exactly like an id that does not exist.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The id of the key to revoke, as returned in the id field when it was issued.

get.description: Every tool that can be submitted, by name.

post.summary: Pack several files into one archive
post.description: ZIP, TAR.GZ, TAR or GZ. The order of file_ids is the order of the entries, and each entry keeps the name its upload had. gz is the exception: it compresses a single stream, so submitting more than one file for it is a validation error rather than an archive holding only the first. XZ and ZSTD are not offered — neither is in the Go standard library, and the four formats here cover what a web service is sent.

file_ids.description: The uploads to pack, in order. One to sixty-four.

idempotency_key.description: Repeat a submission safely: the same key returns the same conversion.

options.description: The format, the compression level and the archive's name. Every field is optional.

post.summary: Unpack an archive into its files
post.description: Each member becomes a result of its own with its own expiry, so all of them have to be downloaded within the result lifetime. The format is read from the archive's bytes rather than its name. Folders are flattened: only a member's filename survives, and two members that then share a name are both kept, numbered. An archive is refused if it holds more than 64 files or unpacks to more than 512 MB, or if any member is a link or a device rather than a file.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours: a ZIP, TAR, TAR.GZ or GZ.

options.description: Extracting has no options: the archive says what it is.

post.summary: Convert audio, or extract a video's soundtrack
post.description: The same operation either way: a video input has its picture dropped and its audio encoded. Loudness normalisation aims at -16 LUFS, the figure streaming platforms use, and the two-pass form measures the whole recording first so it actually hits the target.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours, from the resumable upload endpoint.

idempotency_key.description: Repeat a submission safely: the same key returns the same conversion.

options.description: How to convert. Only the output format is required. A video input has its soundtrack extracted.

get.summary: List the audio formats this server can write
get.description: With whether each one takes a bit rate: FLAC and WAV are lossless and refuse one.

post.summary: Convert a spreadsheet to PDF
post.description: Converted with LibreOffice from the document's own page setup. A font the server does not have is replaced by a similar one, so line breaks can differ from the original application, and macros never run. Linked images that need the network are left out. Each sheet is paginated by its own print settings.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: No options.

post.summary: Make an image smaller without changing what it is
post.description: The format never changes; image-convert is what changes a format. Each mode runs every encoder setting worth trying and keeps the smallest file, so a lossy compression can legitimately come back lossless when that was smaller. A file this encoder cannot beat is returned unchanged with the fact stated, rather than re-encoded into something larger. PNG and GIF compress losslessly by default, JPEG and WebP lossily; lossless is refused for JPEG, because libvips has no lossless JPEG re-encode and jpegtran is not in this image. Metadata is always removed.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours, from the resumable upload endpoint.

idempotency_key.description: Repeat a submission safely: the same key returns the same conversion.

options.description: How hard to compress. Every field is optional.

post.summary: Convert, resize, crop, rotate or flip an image
post.description: One libvips pass does all of it: a resize is a re-encode with a target size, and the orientation and colour handling happen on the same pass. EXIF is removed unless you ask for it, because a photograph's EXIF often carries GPS coordinates and a device serial number.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours, from the resumable upload endpoint.

idempotency_key.description: Repeat a submission safely: the same key returns the same conversion.

options.description: How to convert. Only the output format is required.

get.summary: List the image formats this server can read and write
get.description: Probed from the engine at boot rather than declared. A format whose encoder is not in this build is reported as unwritable, so a client never offers a conversion that would be refused.

post.summary: Bind images into a PDF, one per page
post.description: A JPEG input is embedded exactly as uploaded, re-encoded zero times. Anything else is converted to JPEG once, with transparency flattened onto white. The order of file_ids is the page order.

file_ids.description: The images, in page order. One to fifty.

options.description: Page size, orientation, fit and margin.

post.summary: Compare two PDFs' text, page by page
post.description: Exactly two uploads, the earlier document first. The result is a Markdown report of the lines that differ on each page. It compares text: a change to a font, a margin or a picture does not change the text, so it does not appear.

file_ids.description: Exactly two uploads: the earlier document first.

idempotency_key.description: Repeat a submission safely: the same key returns the same conversion.

options.description: Comparison has no options.

post.summary: Make a PDF smaller
post.description: Three levels, which differ in the resolution images are downsampled to: 300, 150 or 96 DPI. A document that is already smaller than the compressed version is returned unchanged rather than re-encoded into something larger, and the conversion says which happened.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: Which compression level to use.

post.summary: Trim a PDF's margins
post.description: Sets the crop box, which is what a reader displays and prints. The trimmed content is hidden rather than deleted, so the crop can be undone, and everything else about the document is left alone.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: How many points to trim from each edge.

post.summary: Keep only the pages you name
post.description: Pages are named as 1-3,5,8-z, where z is the last page. A page the document does not have is a validation error rather than a page quietly skipped. The bookmarks are dropped, because some would point at pages that are no longer there.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: Which pages to keep.

post.summary: List, fill or flatten a PDF form
post.description: The list action returns every field as JSON: its full name, type (text, checkbox, radio, choice), current value, options and whether it is read-only. The fill action sets the values you give, by field name; a checkbox takes true or false, and a radio group or a choice takes one of its listed options. A field that does not exist, is read-only, or is given a value it cannot hold is refused rather than skipped. The flatten action, or flatten on a fill, turns the form into plain page content. Scripts in the form do not run, so calculated fields are not recalculated.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: What to do with the form, and the values to fill.

post.summary: Join several PDFs into one
post.description: The order of file_ids is the order of the pages. The first document's bookmarks and every document's links are kept; the later documents' bookmarks cannot be, because there is nowhere to graft them on. An encrypted input is refused.

file_ids.description: The uploads to join, in order. Two to fifty.

idempotency_key.description: Repeat a submission safely: the same key returns the same conversion.

options.description: Merging has no options; the order of file_ids is the order of the pages.

post.summary: Make a scanned PDF searchable
post.description: Recognises the text of scanned pages with Tesseract and adds it as an invisible layer, so the document can be searched and copied from. Pages that already have text are left as they are. English and Portuguese are installed; name both for a mixed document. At most 100 pages. Recognition makes mistakes: check names and numbers.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: The languages in the scan.

post.summary: Reorder or duplicate pages
post.description: The page list is the new order, and a page may appear twice. A list that is a pure reordering keeps the bookmarks, because every page is still there; one that drops a page does not.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: The pages in the order they should appear.

post.summary: Stamp page numbers onto a PDF
post.description: The label is a template: {n} is the number and {total} the count, so "Page {n} of {total}" and "- {n} -" both work. Numbering can start at any number and cover a page range, which is what a document with a cover page needs.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: The label, the position and which pages.

post.summary: Encrypt a PDF with a password
post.description: AES-256, with the printing, modification and extraction permissions you choose. The owner password is required, because permissions without one can be removed by any PDF tool. Nobody, including this service, can recover a password you lose.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: The passwords and the permissions.

post.summary: Remove the pages you name
post.description: The inverse of extracting: the pages named are removed and the rest keep their order. Removing every page is refused.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: Which pages to remove.

post.summary: Rebuild a damaged PDF's structure
post.description: Best effort, and honest about the limit: it rebuilds the cross-reference table and the object graph, not content the file no longer holds. A file it cannot rebuild into a readable document is refused rather than returned as a document that opens empty.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: Repair has no options.

post.summary: Rotate pages by 90, 180 or 270 degrees
post.description: By default the rotation is added to each page's own; set absolute to replace it. Nothing else about the document changes: the bookmarks, the links and the page content are untouched.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: How far to rotate, and which pages.

post.summary: Sign a PDF with your own certificate
post.description: Exactly two uploads: the PDF and a .p12 (or .pfx) bundle holding your certificate and private key, with the bundle's password in the options. The signature is an invisible, detached CMS signature (adbe.pkcs7.detached) with SHA-256, RSA or ECDSA, and any PDF reader can verify it. The key is used for this one signature and is not kept: the bundle is deleted with the other uploads when they expire. A self-signed certificate proves the document has not changed since signing, but a reader will not vouch for who signed it until it trusts that certificate; this is not a qualified electronic signature. An expired certificate, an encrypted document, and a document that is already signed are refused, because signing again would invalidate the first signature.

file_ids.description: Exactly two uploads: the PDF and your .p12 certificate bundle, in either order.

idempotency_key.description: Repeat a submission safely: the same key returns the same conversion.

options.description: The bundle's password and what to show beside the signature.

post.summary: Split a PDF into several files
post.description: Either every n pages or by the ranges you name. Every part is a result of its own with its own expiry, so all of them have to be downloaded within the result lifetime. The parts do not carry the original's bookmarks, because a part holds a subset of the pages.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: How to split. Every field is optional.

post.summary: Render pages to PNG or JPEG
post.description: One image per page, at 36 to 600 DPI. Pages are rendered from the crop box, so the image matches what a reader shows rather than the untrimmed sheet.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: Format, resolution and which pages.

post.summary: Convert to the archival PDF/A format
post.description: Targets PDF/A-1b, 2b or 3b. Content is kept in preference to conformance: a document that cannot be made conformant comes back with its pages intact and the converter's own list of what is wrong, rather than conformant with content silently removed.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: Which conformance level to target.

post.summary: Extract a PDF's text, as text or Markdown
post.description: The Markdown form recognises numbered and capitalised headings, bulleted and numbered lists, and joins the extractor's hard-wrapped lines back into paragraphs. It is a text conversion with heuristics, not a layout reconstruction: a document whose headings are marked only by font size comes out as paragraphs, and a table comes out as spaced text. A scanned document has no text to extract.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: Text or Markdown, and which pages.

post.summary: Remove a password you know
post.description: The password you supply is tried exactly once. There is no recovery of a password you do not have and no brute-force path in the code. A wrong password is refused with one message that does not say whether the document had a user password, an owner password or both.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: The password that opens the document.

post.summary: Stamp text across a PDF's pages
post.description: Position, size, angle, opacity and ink are all yours to set. The text is limited to unaccented Latin letters, digits and punctuation, because the standard PDF fonts are the only ones stamped without embedding a font file. A watermark is a visible mark, not protection.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: The text and how to draw it.

post.summary: Turn pixel art into SVG
post.description: Traces an uploaded image into SVG. The upload and the conversion are bound in one transaction, so a conversion always has its input. Send an idempotency_key to make a retry safe.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours, from the resumable upload endpoint.

idempotency_key.description: Repeat a submission safely: the same key returns the same conversion.

options.description: How to convert. Every field is optional.

post.summary: Convert a presentation to PDF
post.description: Converted with LibreOffice from the document's own page setup. A font the server does not have is replaced by a similar one, so line breaks can differ from the original application, and macros never run. Linked images that need the network are left out. One slide is one page.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: No options.

post.summary: Pack frames into a sprite sheet
post.description: Takes a ZIP of frames. The grid layout gives every frame an identical cell and is the default, because it is what Godot 4 and Unity import with no metadata file at all; compact packs frames of differing sizes more tightly. Frames that do not fit are refused with the count that fitted and the size that would be needed, never silently dropped. The packer never rotates a frame.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours: a ZIP of frames.

options.description: How to pack the frames, and which metadata to write.

post.summary: Cut a sprite sheet into frames
post.description: Grid mode cuts the sheet on a grid you describe and is exact; auto mode finds each frame's bounding box from the sheet's own content, which is the answer for a hand-drawn sheet. A fully opaque sheet with no background colour named is refused rather than guessed at. The result is one archive — the frames and the metadata together, so one download is self-contained — plus each metadata file on its own. Trimming is refused with the css format, which has nowhere to record the offset.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours: the sheet to cut.

idempotency_key.description: Repeat a submission safely: the same key returns the same conversion.

options.description: How to find the frames, and which metadata to write.

get.summary: The metadata formats, the modes and the limits
get.description: What sprite-split and sprite-build can produce, with one sentence per metadata format saying what reads it. Published so the interface does not hold a list of its own, which is the only way the two can agree.

post.summary: Cut, crop or split a video
post.description: Trims an uploaded video to a range, crops the frame, or splits it into consecutive clips of up to a minute. A cut that lands on a keyframe is copied rather than re-encoded, which is an order of magnitude cheaper; frame_accurate forces the re-encode. A crop is validated against the real stream dimensions, and a crop outside them is refused with those dimensions named.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours, from the resumable upload endpoint.

idempotency_key.description: Repeat a submission safely: the same key returns the same conversion.

options.description: How to cut. Every field is optional.

post.summary: Make a video or an audio file smaller
post.description: Re-encodes an uploaded file and returns whichever is smaller, the result or the original. When the original wins, the conversion still finishes: bytes_out equals bytes_in and the result is the file you sent, which is the honest answer for something that is already optimal.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours, from the resumable upload endpoint.

idempotency_key.description: Repeat a submission safely: the same key returns the same conversion.

post.summary: Convert a video between containers and codecs
post.description: Progress is reported on the conversion's event stream. A codec the container cannot carry usefully, or that this build cannot encode, is refused here rather than by the engine a minute later.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours, from the resumable upload endpoint.

idempotency_key.description: Repeat a submission safely: the same key returns the same conversion.

options.description: How to convert. Only the container is required; the codecs default to the ones that container plays everywhere.

get.summary: List the containers and codecs this server can produce
get.description: H.264 and H.265 come from x264 and x265, which are GPL-only, so an ffmpeg built without GPL support has neither. gpl_build says which build this is, and codecs lists what can actually be encoded.

post.summary: Download a video from a URL
post.description: Fetches a video from YouTube, Instagram, X or TikTok. This is the one conversion with no upload: the input is the URL, so bytes_in is 0 until the download has happened. Ask for audio to get MP3, for clips to get consecutive segments delivered individually and as a zip, and for compression to have the result re-encoded and whichever file is smaller delivered. Downloading may breach a platform's terms of service and you are responsible for what you download.

idempotency_key.description: Repeat a submission safely: the same key returns the same conversion.

options.description: What to download and how.

post.summary: Report what a platform says about a URL
post.description: The title, the uploader, the duration, the thumbnail, the available formats and the expected size, without downloading anything. The size cap is checked against estimated_bytes, so too_large tells you the download will be refused before you submit it. A POST rather than a GET because a URL in a query string ends up in every log between here and the caller.

url.description: A YouTube, Instagram, X or TikTok URL.

post.summary: Turn part of a video into an animated GIF
post.description: Two passes: a palette is computed from the frames in the clip and the frames are then mapped onto it, which is the difference between a GIF that looks like the video and one that bands. Capped at 15 seconds, because a GIF's size grows linearly with its duration.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours, from the resumable upload endpoint.

idempotency_key.description: Repeat a submission safely: the same key returns the same conversion.

options.description: Which part of the video, and how. Every field is optional.

post.summary: Convert a Word or OpenDocument text file to PDF
post.description: Converted with LibreOffice from the document's own page setup. A font the server does not have is replaced by a similar one, so line breaks can differ from the original application, and macros never run. Linked images that need the network are left out.

file_id.description: The id of an upload of yours.

options.description: No options.

get.summary: List the file types an upload may have
get.description: Every type the service accepts at the door, so a client does not hardcode them.
Uploads of yours that no conversion has claimed yet, newest first. A resumable upload has no response body, so this is how a client learns the id of the upload it just finished.
What the account has spent today and what is left, in seconds of processing time, and when the budget resets. unlimited is true when no daily budget applies.

data.description: Every ability a key may be granted.

format.description: zip, tar.gz, tar or gz. Default zip.

level.description: Compression level, 1 to 9. 0 uses the format's default.

name.description: The archive's name, without an extension. Default archive.

formats.description: Every output format, with whether this server can write it.

loudness_target.description: The integrated loudness normalisation aims at, in LUFS.

max_seconds.description: The longest recording this server converts, in seconds.

readable.description: The media types this server accepts, including video, since extracting a soundtrack is the same conversion.

sample_rates.description: The sample rates a conversion may ask for. 0 keeps the source's.

writable.description: The formats this server can write, by name.

bitrate.description: Bit rate in kbit/s for MP3, Opus and AAC. 0 uses the format's default. Ignored by FLAC and WAV, which are lossless.

channels.description: 1 for mono, 2 for stereo. 0 keeps the source's.

sample_rate.description: Resample, in hertz. 0 keeps the source's rate.

to.description: mp3, wav, flac, opus or aac. GET /api/v1/tools/audio-convert/formats lists what this server can write.

two_pass.description: Measure the whole recording before correcting it. Costs a second decode and is the only way to hit the target reliably.

extension.description: The canonical extension, with the dot.

label.description: What to call it in an interface.

lossy.description: Whether a bit rate applies. FLAC and WAV are lossless and refuse one.

mime.description: The media type a file of this format has.

name.description: The identifier to send as options.to.

write.description: Whether this server can produce it.

engines.name: ffmpeg
engines.version: ffmpeg version 7.1.5-0+deb13u1 Copyright (c) 2000-2026 the FFmpeg developers

engines.name: ffprobe
engines.version: ffprobe version 7.1.5-0+deb13u1 Copyright (c) 2007-2026 the FFmpeg developers

engines.description: Every external program, and whether this server has it.

tools.description: Every tool that can be submitted.

clip_seconds.description: Clip length in seconds for split mode, 1 to 60. Default 60.

crop.description: The area to keep, in pixels. Leave it out to keep the whole frame.

duration_seconds.description: How much to keep, in seconds. 0 means to the end.

error_type.description: A code from the error taxonomy, empty unless it failed.

expires_at.description: When the result stops being downloadable.

id.description: The conversion id, used to poll it, stream it or cancel it.

note.description: What the conversion did, in its own words. Empty when the file says it all.

phase.description: What it is doing now, empty once it has ended.

started_at.description: When a worker picked it up, or null.

status.description: One of pending, running, finished, error, cancelled.

clip_seconds.description: Clip length in seconds, 1 to 60. Default 60.

clips.description: Split the result into consecutive clips, delivered individually and as a zip.

compress.description: Compress afterwards and keep whichever file is smaller.

kind.description: video keeps the picture, audio gives MP3. Default video.

url.description: A YouTube, Instagram, X or TikTok URL.

present.description: Whether it was resolved at startup.

version.description: The version it reported, empty when absent.

mime.description: The media type a file of this format has.

name.description: The identifier to send as options.to.

read.description: Whether this server can read it.

write.description: Whether this server can produce it.

fit.description: contain fits inside the margins, fill covers the page, exact makes the page the image's own size. Default contain.

margin.description: Points of space around the image, 0 to 144. Default 0.

orientation.description: auto turns each page to match its image. Also portrait or landscape. Default auto.

page_size.description: a4, a3, a5, letter or legal. Default a4.

quality.description: Quality for images that have to be converted, 1 to 100. Default 90. A JPEG input is never re-encoded.

max_clip_seconds.description: The longest clip a split produces.

max_clips.description: The most clips one conversion delivers.

max_download_bytes.description: The largest download allowed, 0 for no cap.

max_output_seconds.description: The longest output a cut produces, 0 for no cap.

device_code.description: Secret to poll with. Never show it to the person.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the link can no longer be approved.

user_code.description: The short code to show the person, formatted XXXX-XXXX.

verification_url.description: Where the person approves. It already contains the user code.

abilities.description: What the key may do. Only when approved.

expires_at.description: When the key stops working. Only when approved.

id.description: The key id, used to revoke it. Only when approved.

status.description: pending, approved, denied or expired. A link that never existed reads as expired.

token.description: The secret key, shown once. Only when approved.

type.description: The authorization scheme, always Bearer. Only when approved.

formats.description: Every image format, with whether this server can read it, write it, or both.

readable.description: The media types this server accepts as input.

rotations.description: The quarter turns a client may ask for.

writable.description: The formats this server can write, by name.

bitrate_kbps.description: Its total bitrate in kilobits per second.

bytes.description: Its size, 0 when the platform does not say.

resolution.description: Its frame size, empty for an audio-only stream.

estimated_bytes.description: The expected size at best quality. The cap is checked against this for quality=best.

max_bytes.description: The largest download this server allows.

smallest_bytes.description: The expected size at quality=smallest, 0 when the platform declares none.

thumbnail.description: A link to the platform's own thumbnail.

title.description: The video's title, as the platform gives it.

too_large.description: Whether even the smallest stream is past the cap.

data.description: The accepted values, in the order to show them.

level.description: light keeps every page's appearance, balanced is the default, strong is for email.

bottom.description: Points to trim from the bottom edge.

left.description: Points to trim from the left edge.

pages.description: Pages to crop, as 1-3,5. Empty crops every page.

right.description: Points to trim from the right edge.

top.description: Points to trim from the top edge.

name.description: The field's full name, as the list action reports it.

value.description: The value. A checkbox takes true or false; a radio group or a choice takes one of its options.

action.description: list reports the fields as JSON; fill sets the values given; flatten turns the form into plain page content. Default list.

flatten.description: Flatten the form after filling it, so the values can no longer be edited.

values.description: The fields to fill, for the fill action.

deskew.description: Straighten pages that were scanned at a slight angle.

languages.description: Languages in the scan: eng, por. Several may be combined. Default eng.

format.description: The label, with {n} for the number and {total} for the count. Default {n}.

pages.description: Pages to number, as 2-z. Empty numbers every page.

size.description: Font size in points, 4 to 144. Default 10.

start_at.description: The number on the first numbered page. Default 1.

pages.description: Pages, as 1-3,5,8-z. z is the last page.

allow_extract.description: Allow text to be copied out. Screen-reader access is always allowed.

modify.description: all, annotate, form, assembly or none. Default all.

owner_password.description: The password that lifts the restrictions. Required, and must differ from the opening password.

print.description: full, low or none. Default full.

user_password.description: The password needed to open the document. Leave empty to restrict permissions only.

absolute.description: Set the rotation rather than add to the page's current one.

pages.description: Pages to rotate, as 1-3,5. Empty rotates every page.

contact.description: How to reach the signer. Optional.

password.description: The password of the .p12 certificate bundle. The key is used for this one signature and is not kept.

reason.description: Why you are signing. Shown beside the signature. Optional.

every.description: Pages per file, for the every mode. Default 1.

mode.description: every splits into groups of n pages; ranges uses the ranges given. Default every.

ranges.description: One range per output file, for the ranges mode.

pages.description: Pages to render, as 1-3,5. Empty renders every page.

part.description: PDF/A conformance: 1 for 1b, 2 for 2b, 3 for 3b. Default 2.

layout.description: Keep the page's column spacing, for the text format.

page_rules.description: Write a rule between pages, for the markdown format.

pages.description: One continuous range such as 1-20. Empty reads the whole document.

password.description: The password that opens the document. It is tried once; there is no recovery of a password you do not have.

pages.description: Pages to stamp, as 1-3,5. Empty stamps every page.

position.description: top-left to bottom-right, or center. Default center.

rotate.description: Angle in degrees anticlockwise. 45 is the usual diagonal.

size.description: Font size in points, 4 to 144. 0 picks a size from the page width.

text.description: The text to stamp. Unaccented Latin letters, digits and punctuation.

alpha.description: opacity keeps partial transparency, drop removes it. Default opacity.

max_colors.description: Palette cap, 1 to 256. 0 uses the default, -1 means no reduction.

mode.description: square, rect or contour. Default rect.

scale.description: Multiplies the rendered size. 0 and 1 both mean actual size.

simplify.description: Contour simplification in pixels, contour mode only. 0 keeps it pixel-exact.

tolerance.description: Merge colours closer than this (0 to 255). 0 disables merging.

data.description: Every platform a URL may belong to.

hosts.description: The domains a URL may be on.

label.description: What to call it in an interface.

name.description: The stable id, as a conversion reports it.

expires_at.description: When the file is deleted and the link stops working.

name.description: The file name to save it as.

url.description: A signed link, valid until expires_at and no longer.

aseprite.description: Add Aseprite's per-frame duration and frameTags to the JSON formats.

extrude.description: Repeat each frame's edge pixels into the padding, which is the fix for the dark halo transparent padding leaves.

frame_ms.description: Per-frame duration in milliseconds for the Aseprite extensions. 0 means 100.

layout.description: grid or compact. Default grid, which Godot 4 and Unity import with no metadata file.

margin.description: Transparent gutter at the sheet's edges.

max_size.description: Cap the sheet's width and height. 0 means 4096, which every GPU handles as one texture.

metadata.description: Metadata formats to write, at most four.

padding.description: Transparent gutter between two frames, which stops a neighbour's colour bleeding in.

pot.description: Round the sheet up to a power of two on both axes.

formats.imports: Phaser 3 (load.atlas) and PixiJS. The usual choice for a web game.
formats.name: json-hash

formats.imports: A web page, as a CSS sprite sheet: one class per frame. Cannot express trimming.
formats.name: css

formats.description: Every metadata format, in the order the interface offers them.

max_formats.description: How many metadata formats one conversion may ask for.

max_frames.description: The most frames one conversion produces.

max_size.description: The largest sheet dimension, in pixels.

extension.description: The file's extension, with the dot.

imports.description: One sentence saying what reads this format.

mime.description: The media type the result is served as.

name.description: The value to send in options.metadata.

trim.description: Whether the format can describe a trimmed frame. CSS cannot.

aseprite.description: Add Aseprite's per-frame duration and frameTags to the JSON formats.

background.description: Hex colour auto mode treats as empty, e.g. #ff00ff. Empty means transparency.

background_tolerance.description: How far a pixel may be from the background colour and still count as background.

cell_w.description: Cell width in pixels. Give this and cell_h, or cols and rows.

cols.description: Column count, as an alternative to the cell size.

frame_ms.description: Per-frame duration in milliseconds for the Aseprite extensions. 0 means 100.

margin.description: Gutter between the sheet's edge and the first cell.

metadata.description: Metadata formats to write, at most four. GET /api/v1/tools/sprite-split/formats lists them.

min_frame.description: Drop a detected frame smaller than this many pixels, as noise. Auto mode only.

prefix.description: Frame name prefix; the nth frame is prefix plus a zero-padded index. Default frame.

trim.description: Shrink each frame to its opaque box, recording the offset so an importer can re-inflate it. Refused with the css metadata format, which has nowhere to put the offset.

expires_at.description: When the key stops working, or null when it never expires.

id.description: The key id, used to revoke it.

token.description: The secret key. It is shown once; store it now.

type.description: The authorization scheme to use, always "Bearer".

data.description: The caller's keys, newest first, revoked ones included.
Every tool that can be submitted, by name.
Every MIME type an upload may have.
Your uploads that no conversion has claimed yet, newest first.

expires_at.description: When an unused upload is deleted.

id.description: Use this as file_id when submitting a conversion.

mime.description: The type detected from the bytes, not from the name.

budget_seconds.description: Today's budget in seconds of processing time. 0 when unlimited.

remaining_seconds.description: What is left today, in seconds. 0 when unlimited or spent: read unlimited to tell them apart.

resets_at.description: When the next day's budget starts (midnight UTC).

spent_seconds.description: Processing time spent today, in seconds.

stored_bytes.description: Bytes of yours that are stored and have not expired: uploads and results.

stored_limit_bytes.description: The most bytes an account may store at once. 0 when there is no cap.

unlimited.description: True when no daily budget applies to this account.

codecs.description: The video codecs this server can encode. An ffmpeg built without GPL support has no H.264 or H.265.

containers.description: Every output container, with the codecs it carries.

gpl_build.description: Whether the video engine is built with GPL support, which H.264 and H.265 require.

max_gif_seconds.description: The longest range video-to-gif will convert, in seconds.

max_seconds.description: The longest video this server converts, in seconds.

audio_codecs.description: The audio codecs this container carries here, plus copy and mute.

extension.description: The canonical extension, with the dot.

label.description: What to call it in an interface.

name.description: The identifier to send as options.container.

video_codecs.description: The video codecs this container carries here.

audio.description: aac, opus, mp3, flac, vorbis, copy or mute. Empty uses the container's default.

audio_bitrate.description: Audio bit rate in kbit/s. 0 uses the codec's default.

crf.description: Quality on the codec's own scale; the scales are not comparable between codecs. 0 uses the codec's default.

frame_rate.description: Cap the frame rate. 0 leaves it alone.

height.description: Scale to this height, keeping the shape. Only downwards. 0 leaves the resolution alone.

video.description: h264, h265, vp9 or av1. Empty uses the container's default. GET /api/v1/tools/video-convert/capabilities lists what this server has.

duration_seconds.description: How long, in seconds. 0 takes the rest of the video, up to the 15 second limit.

fps.description: Frames per second. 0 uses 12, which divides 100 evenly and so plays evenly.

width.description: Width in pixels. 0 uses 480: a GIF has no interframe compression, so doubling the width quadruples the file.

ValidationError.description: Validation failed; errors maps each field to its messages and issues lists each problem with its code, key and params

apiKey.description: The same API key in the `X-API-Key` header. `Authorization` wins when both are sent.
apiKey.name: X-API-Key

bearer.description: An API key from POST /api/v1/tokens, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
